text: Let $\mathrm{A}=\{-3,-2,-1,0,1,2,3\}$ and R be a relation on A defined by $x\mathrm{R}y$ if and only if $2x-y\in \{0,1\}$. Let $l$ be the number of elements in $R$. Let $m$ and $n$ be the minimum number of elements required to be added in R to make it reflexive and symmetric relations, respectively. Then $l+\mathrm{m}+\mathrm{n}$ is equal to:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\begin{array}{l} \begin{array}{l} xRy⇔2x-y\in \{0,1\} \\ \Rightarrow y=2x\text{or}y=2x-1 \\ A=\{-3,-2,-1,0,1,2,3\} \\ \mathrm{R}=\{(-1,-2),(0,0),(1,2),(-1,-3),(0,-1),(1,1), \\ (2,3)\} \\ \Rightarrow l=7 \end{array} \\ \text{For}R\text{to be reflexive}(0,0),(1,1)\in R \end{array}$

But other $(a,a)$ such that $2a-a\in \{0,1\}$

$\Rightarrow \quad a\in \{0,1\}$

5 other pairs need to be added $\Rightarrow m=5$

$xRy\Rightarrow yRx$ to be symmetric

$(-1,-2)\Rightarrow (-2,-1)$

$(1,2)\Rightarrow (2,1)$

$(-1,-3)\Rightarrow (-3,-1)$

$(0,-1)\Rightarrow (-1,0)$

$(2,3)\Rightarrow (3,2)\Rightarrow 5$ needs to be added, $n=5$

$\Rightarrow \quad l+m+n=17$

text: Let the mean and the standard deviation of the observation $2,3,3,4,5,7,a,b$ be 4 and $\sqrt{2}$ respectively. Then the mean deviation about the mode of these observations is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\begin{array}{l} \begin{array}{l} \dfrac{2+3+3+4+5+7+a+b}{8}=4 \\ \Rightarrow a+b=8 \\ (\sqrt{2})^{2}=\dfrac{2^{2}+3^{2}+3^{2}+4^{2}+5^{2}+7^{2}+a^{2}+b^{2}}{8}-16 \\ 112+a^{2}+b^{2}=18\times 8 \\ \Rightarrow a^{2}+b^{2}=32 \\ \Rightarrow a=b=4 \end{array} \\ \text{Now numbers be} \\ 2,3,3,4,4,4,5,7 \end{array}$

Mode $=4$

Mean deviation about mode :

$\begin{array}{ll} \dfrac{|2-4|+|3-4|+|3-4|+0+0+0+|5-4|+|4-7|}{8} \\ = & \dfrac{2+1+1+1+3}{8}=\dfrac{8}{8}=1 \end{array}$

text: Let the sum of the focal distances of the point $\mathrm{P}(4,3)$ on the hyperbola $\mathrm{H}:\frac{x^{2}}{\mathrm{a}^{2}}-\frac{y^{2}}{\mathrm{b}^{2}}=1$ be $8\sqrt{\frac{5}{3}}$. If for H , the length of the latus rectum is $l$ and the product of the focal distances of the point P is m , then $9l^{2}+6\mathrm{m}$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For a point $(x_{1},y_{1})$ on the right branch of $\dfrac{x^{2}}{a^{2}}-\dfrac{y^{2}}{b^{2}}=1$, the focal distances are $ex_{1}+a$ and $ex_{1}-a$.

For $\mathrm{P}(4,3)$ their sum is $2e(4)=8e=8\sqrt{\dfrac{5}{3}}$, so $e^{2}=\dfrac{5}{3}$ and $b^{2}=a^{2}(e^{2}-1)=\dfrac{2a^{2}}{3}$.

P lies on H:

$\frac{16}{a^{2}}-\frac{9}{b^{2}}=1\Rightarrow \frac{16}{a^{2}}-\frac{27}{2a^{2}}=1\Rightarrow \frac{5}{2a^{2}}=1\Rightarrow a^{2}=\frac{5}{2},b^{2}=\frac{5}{3}$

Latus rectum: $l=\dfrac{2b^{2}}{a}$, so

$9l^{2}=\frac{36b^{4}}{a^{2}}=\frac{36\times \frac{25}{9}}{\frac{5}{2}}=40$

Product of focal distances:

$m=(ex_{1}+a)(ex_{1}-a)=e^{2}x_{1}^{2}-a^{2}=\frac{5}{3}(16)-\frac{5}{2}=\frac{145}{6}\Rightarrow 6m=145$

$9l^{2}+6m=40+145=185$

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift

text: Let the matrix $A=\left [\begin{array}{lll} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \end{array}\right ]$ satisfy $A^{n}=A^{n-2}+A^{2}-I$ for $n⩾3$. Then the sum of all the elements of $\mathrm{A}^{50}$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given $A=\left [\begin{array}{lll} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \end{array}\right ]$,

$A^{2}=\left [\begin{array}{lll} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 1 \end{array}\right ],A^{2}-I=\left [\begin{array}{lll} 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 \end{array}\right ].$

For even $n$, the relation $A^{n}=A^{n-2}+(A^{2}-I)$ gives $A^{4}=A^{2}+(A^{2}-I)$, $A^{6}=A^{4}+(A^{2}-I)=A^{2}+2(A^{2}-I)$, and in general

$A^{2k}=A^{2}+(k-1)(A^{2}-I).$

For $2k=50$, $k=25$:

$A^{50}=A^{2}+24(A^{2}-I)=\left [\begin{array}{lll} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 1+24 & 1 & 0 \\ 1+24 & 0 & 1 \end{array}\right ]=\left [\begin{array}{lll} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 25 & 1 & 0 \\ 25 & 0 & 1 \end{array}\right ].$

Sum of all elements $=1+25+1+25+1=53$.

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift

text: If a curve $y=y(x)$ passes through the point $\left (1,\frac{π}{2}\right )$ and satisfies the differential equation $\left (7x^{4}\cot y-\mathrm{e}^{x}\mathrm{cosec}y\right )\frac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}y}=x^{5},x\geq 1$, then at $x=2$, the value of $\cos y$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\begin{array}{l} \left (7x^{4}\cot y-e^{x}\mathrm{cosec}y\right )\dfrac{dx}{dy}=x^{5} \\ x^{5}\dfrac{dy}{dx}-7x^{4}\cot y=-e^{x}\mathrm{cosec}y \\ \dfrac{dy}{dx}-\dfrac{7}{x}\cot y=-\dfrac{e^{x}}{x^{5}}\mathrm{cosec}y \\ \sin y\dfrac{dy}{dx}-\dfrac{7}{x}\cos y=-\dfrac{e^{x}}{x^{5}} \\ \text{Let}-\cos y=t \\ \sin y\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{dt}{dx} \\ \therefore \dfrac{dt}{dx}+\dfrac{7}{x}t=-\dfrac{e^{x}}{x^{5}} \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{l} \therefore \text{I.F.}=e^{\int \frac{7}{x}dx}=x^{7} \\ t\cdot x^{7}=\int \dfrac{-e^{x}}{x^{5}}\cdot x^{7}dx \\ -\cos y\cdot x^{7}=-\int e^{x}x^{2}dx \\ \cos yx^{7}=e^{x}\left (x^{2}-2x+2\right )+c \\ \because \quad x=1\text{then}y=\dfrac{π}{2}\Rightarrow c=-e \\ \therefore \quad \cos y\cdot x^{7}=e^{x}\left (x^{2}-2x+2\right )-e \\ \text{When}x=2\text{then}\cos y=\dfrac{2e^{2}-e}{128} \end{array}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift

If the sum of the first 20 terms of the series

solution.body: $\begin{array}{l} S_{n}=\sum\limits _{r=1}^{n}\dfrac{4r}{4+3r^{2}+r^{4}} \\ =2\sum\limits _{r=1}^{n}\dfrac{2r}{(r^{2}+2)^{2}-r^{2}}=2\sum\limits _{r=1}^{n}\dfrac{\left (r^{2}+2+r\right )-\left (r^{2}+2-r\right )}{(r^{2}+2+r)(r^{2}+2-r)} \\ =2\sum\limits _{r=1}^{n}\left (\dfrac{1}{r^{2}+2-r}-\dfrac{1}{r^{2}+2+r}\right ) \\ S_{20}=2\left [\left (\dfrac{1}{2}-\dfrac{1}{4}\right )+\left (\dfrac{1}{4}-\dfrac{1}{8}\right )+\ldots \right ] \\ =2\left (\dfrac{1}{2}-\dfrac{1}{20^{2}+2+20}\right ) \\ =2\left (\dfrac{1}{2}-\dfrac{1}{422}\right ) \\ =2\left (\dfrac{422-2}{422\times 2}\right )=\dfrac{420}{422}=\dfrac{210}{211}=\dfrac{m}{n} \\ m+n=421 \end{array}$

text: The centre of a circle C is at the centre of the ellipse $\mathrm{E}:\frac{x^{2}}{\mathrm{a}^{2}}+\frac{y^{2}}{\mathrm{b}^{2}}=1,\mathrm{a}>\mathrm{b}$. Let C pass through the foci $F_{1}$ and $F_{2}$ of E such that the circle $C$ and the ellipse $E$ intersect at four points. Let P be one of these four points. If the area of the triangle $\mathrm{PF}_{1}\mathrm{F}_{2}$ is 30 and the length of the major axis of $E$ is 17 , then the distance between the foci of $E$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The circle $C$ has its centre at the centre of $E$ and passes through the foci $F_{1},F_{2}$, so $F_{1}F_{2}$ is a diameter of $C$. Every point $P$ common to $C$ and $E$ therefore satisfies $\angle F_{1}PF_{2}=90^{\circ }$.

Let $PF_{1}=r_{1}$, $PF_{2}=r_{2}$ and $F_{1}F_{2}=2c$. Since $P$ lies on $E$, $r_{1}+r_{2}=2a=17$.

The area of the right triangle $PF_{1}F_{2}$ gives $\dfrac{1}{2}r_{1}r_{2}=30\Rightarrow r_{1}r_{2}=60$.

By Pythagoras in triangle $PF_{1}F_{2}$:

$(2c)^{2}=r_{1}^{2}+r_{2}^{2}=(r_{1}+r_{2})^{2}-2r_{1}r_{2}=289-120=169$

So the distance between the foci is $2c=13$.

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift

text: Let the product of $ω_{1}=(8+i)\sin θ+(7+4i)\cos θ$ and $ω_{2}=(1+8i)\sin θ+(4+7i)\cos θ$ be $α+iβ$, $i=\sqrt{-1}$. Let p and q be the maximum and the minimum values of $α+β$ respectively. Then $\mathrm{p}+\mathrm{q}$ is equal to :

solution.body:
Let $A=8\sin θ+7\cos θ$ and $B=\sin θ+4\cos θ$. Then

$ω_{1}=A+iB,ω_{2}=B+iA$

$ω_{1}ω_{2}=AB+iA^{2}+iB^{2}+i^{2}AB=i(A^{2}+B^{2})$

so $α=0$ and $β=A^{2}+B^{2}$.

$A^{2}+B^{2}=(64+1)\sin ^{2}θ+(49+16)\cos ^{2}θ+(112+8)\sin θ\cos θ=65+60\sin 2θ$

So $α+β=65+60\sin 2θ$, with maximum $p=125$ and minimum $q=5$, giving $p+q=130$.

Hence, the correct option is (A).

text: The sum of the infinite series $\cot ^{-1}\left (\frac{7}{4}\right )+\cot ^{-1}\left (\frac{19}{4}\right )+\cot ^{-1}\left (\frac{39}{4}\right )+\cot ^{-1}\left (\frac{67}{4}\right )+\ldots$. is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The general term is $T_{r}=\cot ^{-1}\left (\dfrac{4r^{2}+3}{4}\right )$, since $r=1,2,3,4$ give $\dfrac{7}{4},\dfrac{19}{4},\dfrac{39}{4},\dfrac{67}{4}$.

$T_{r}=\tan ^{-1}\dfrac{4}{4r^{2}+3}=\tan ^{-1}\dfrac{1}{1+\left (r^{2}-\frac{1}{4}\right )}=\tan ^{-1}\dfrac{\left (r+\frac{1}{2}\right )-\left (r-\frac{1}{2}\right )}{1+\left (r+\frac{1}{2}\right )\left (r-\frac{1}{2}\right )}$

$\Rightarrow T_{r}=\tan ^{-1}\left (r+\dfrac{1}{2}\right )-\tan ^{-1}\left (r-\dfrac{1}{2}\right )$

The sum of the first $n$ terms telescopes:

$S_{n}=\sum\limits _{r=1}^{n}T_{r}=\tan ^{-1}\left (n+\dfrac{1}{2}\right )-\tan ^{-1}\left (\dfrac{1}{2}\right )$

As $n\to \infty$, $\tan ^{-1}\left (n+\dfrac{1}{2}\right )\to \dfrac{π}{2}$, so

$S_{\infty }=\dfrac{π}{2}-\tan ^{-1}\left (\dfrac{1}{2}\right )$

This value equals $\cot ^{-1}\left (\dfrac{1}{2}\right )=\tan ^{-1}2$; option (B) equals $\tan ^{-1}\left (\dfrac{1}{2}\right )$, and (A), (D) exceed $\dfrac{π}{2}$.

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift

text: Let $f(x)+2f\left (\frac{1}{x}\right )=x^{2}+5$ and $2g(x)-3g\left (\frac{1}{2}\right )=x,x>0$. If $α=\int\limits _{1}^{2}f(x)\mathrm{d}x$, and $β=\int\limits _{1}^{2}g(x)\mathrm{d}x$, then the value of $9α+β$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\begin{array}{l} f(x)+2f\left (\dfrac{1}{x}\right )=x^{2}+5 \\ 2f\left (\dfrac{1}{x}\right )+4f(x)=2\left (\dfrac{1}{x^{2}}+5\right ) \\ 3f(x)=\dfrac{2}{x^{2}}-x^{2}+5 \\ f(x)=\dfrac{1}{3}\left (\dfrac{2}{x^{2}}-x^{2}+5\right ) \\ 2g(x)-3g\left (\dfrac{1}{x}\right )=x \\ 2g\left (\dfrac{1}{x}\right )-3g(x)=\dfrac{1}{x} \\ \text{Or}4g(x)-6g\left (\dfrac{1}{x}\right )=2x \\ 6g\left (\dfrac{1}{x}\right )-9g(x)=\dfrac{3}{x} \\ -5g(x)=2x+\dfrac{3}{x} \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{l} \text{Or}g(x)=-\dfrac{1}{5}\left (2x+\dfrac{3}{x}\right ) \\ \int\limits _{1}^{2}f(x)dx=\int\limits _{1}^{2}\dfrac{1}{3}\left (\dfrac{2}{x^{2}}-x^{2}+5\right )dx \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{l} \begin{array}{l} =\dfrac{1}{3}\left [-\dfrac{2}{x}-\dfrac{x^{3}}{3}+5x\right ]_{1}^{2} \\ =\dfrac{1}{3}\left [\left (-\dfrac{2}{2}-\dfrac{8}{3}+10\right )-\left (-2-\dfrac{1}{3}+5\right )\right ] \\ =\dfrac{1}{3}\left [-1-\dfrac{8}{3}+10+2+\dfrac{1}{3}-5\right ] \\ α=\dfrac{11}{9} \end{array} \\ \text{Now,}2g(x)=x+3g\left (\dfrac{1}{2}\right ) \\ \begin{array}{l} 2g\left (\dfrac{1}{2}\right )=\dfrac{1}{2}+3g\left (\dfrac{1}{2}\right ) \\ g\left (\dfrac{1}{2}\right )=-\dfrac{1}{2} \end{array} \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{l} \therefore β=\int\limits _{1}^{2}g(x)dx \\ =\dfrac{1}{2}\int\limits _{1}^{2}\left (x+3g\left (\dfrac{1}{2}\right )\right )dx \\ =\dfrac{1}{2}\left [\dfrac{x^{2}}{2}+3g\left (\dfrac{1}{2}\right )x\right ]_{1}^{2} \\ =0 \\ \therefore 9α+β=11 \end{array}$

text:
Consider two sets A and B, each containing three numbers in A.P. Let the sum and the product of the elements of A be 36 and p respectively and the sum and the product of the elements of B be 36 and $q$ respectively. Let d and D be the common differences of $\mathrm{AP}^{'}\mathrm{s}$ in
$A$ and $B$ respectively such that $D=d+3,d>0$. If $\frac{p+q}{p-q}=\frac{19}{5}$, then $\mathrm{p}-\mathrm{q}$ is equal to
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let the terms in $A$ be $a_{1}-d,a_{1},a_{1}+d$

and in $B$ be $a_{2}-D,a_{2},a_{2}+D$

Now $3a_{1}=36$

$\Rightarrow \quad a_{1}=12$

and $3a_{2}=36$

$\Rightarrow \quad a_{2}=12$

Now $(12-d)(12)(12+d)=p$

and $(12-D)(12)(12+D)=q$

Also $\frac{p+q}{p-q}=\frac{19}{5}$

$\begin{array}{l} \Rightarrow 12q=7p \\ \Rightarrow 12(12-D)(12)(12+D)=7(12-d)(12)(12+\mathrm{d}) \\ \Rightarrow 12(9-d)(12)(15+d)=7(12-d)(12)(12+\mathrm{d}) \\ \Rightarrow 12\left (135-d^{2}-6d\right )=7\left (144-d^{2}\right ) \\ \Rightarrow d=6,D=9 \\ p=6\times 12\times 18=1296 \\ q=756 \\ p-q=540 \end{array}$

text: Let the values of p , for which the shortest distance between the lines $\frac{x+1}{3}=\frac{y}{4}=\frac{z}{5}$ and $\vec{\mathrm{r}}=(\mathrm{p}\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+\hat{k})+λ(2\hat{i}+3\hat{j}+4\hat{k})$ is $\frac{1}{\sqrt{6}}$, be $\mathrm{a},\mathrm{b},(\mathrm{a}<\mathrm{b})$. Then the length of the latus rectum of the ellipse $\frac{x^{2}}{\mathrm{a}^{2}}+\frac{y^{2}}{\mathrm{b}^{2}}=1$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The first line passes through $(-1,0,0)$ with direction $⃗{b}_{1}=3\hat{i}+4\hat{j}+5\hat{k}$; the second passes through $(p,2,1)$ with direction $⃗{b}_{2}=2\hat{i}+3\hat{j}+4\hat{k}$.

$⃗{b}_{1}\times ⃗{b}_{2}=\left |\begin{array}{lll} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ 3 & 4 & 5 \\ 2 & 3 & 4 \end{array}\right |=\hat{i}-2\hat{j}+\hat{k},|⃗{b}_{1}\times ⃗{b}_{2}|=\sqrt{6}$

The vector joining the two given points is $(p+1)\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+\hat{k}$, so

$d=\frac{|(p+1)-4+1|}{\sqrt{6}}=\frac{|p-2|}{\sqrt{6}}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{6}}\Rightarrow |p-2|=1\Rightarrow p=1,3$

Thus $a=1$, $b=3$ and the ellipse is $\dfrac{x^{2}}{1}+\dfrac{y^{2}}{9}=1$.

Since $b>a$, the major axis lies along the $y$-axis with semi-major axis $3$ and semi-minor axis $1$. The latus rectum equals twice the square of the semi-minor axis divided by the semi-major axis:

$\text{LR}=\frac{2a^{2}}{b}=\frac{2\cdot 1^{2}}{3}=\frac{2}{3}$

Hence, the correct option is (D).

solution.body: $\begin{array}{l} \begin{array}{l} \lim _{x\to 0}(f(2+x))^{3/x}=(1^{\infty }\text{form}) \\ e^{\lim _{x\to 0}\frac{3}{x}(f(2+x)-1)}=e^{\lim _{x\to 0}3f^{'}(2+x)} \\ =e^{3f^{'}(2)} \\ =e^{12} \\ \Rightarrow α=12 \\ y=4x^{3}-4x^{2}-4(12-7)x-12 \\ y=4x^{3}-4x^{2}-20x-12 \\ y=4\left (x^{3}-x^{2}-5x-3\right ) \\ =4(x+1)^{2}(x-3) \end{array} \\ \text{It meets the}x\text{-axis at two points} \end{array}$

text: If $\int \frac{\left (\sqrt{1+x^{2}}+x\right )^{10}}{\left (\sqrt{1+x^{2}}-x\right )^{9}}\mathrm{d}x=\frac{1}{\mathrm{m}}\left (\left (\sqrt{1+x^{2}}+x\right )^{\mathrm{n}}\left (\mathrm{n}\sqrt{1+x^{2}}-x\right )\right )+\mathrm{C}$ where C is the constant of integration and $\mathrm{m},\mathrm{n}\in 𝐍$, then $\mathrm{m}+\mathrm{n}$ is equal to $_________$ .
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let $t=\sqrt{1+x^{2}}+x$. Then $\sqrt{1+x^{2}}-x=\dfrac{1}{t}$, so the integrand is $t^{10}\cdot t^{9}=t^{19}$.

From $t-\dfrac{1}{t}=2x$ and $t+\dfrac{1}{t}=2\sqrt{1+x^{2}}$: $x=\dfrac{t^{2}-1}{2t}$, $\sqrt{1+x^{2}}=\dfrac{t^{2}+1}{2t}$ and $dx=\dfrac{1}{2}\left (1+\dfrac{1}{t^{2}}\right )dt=\dfrac{t^{2}+1}{2t^{2}}dt$.

$I=\int t^{19}\cdot \dfrac{t^{2}+1}{2t^{2}}dt=\dfrac{1}{2}\int \left (t^{19}+t^{17}\right )dt=\dfrac{t^{20}}{40}+\dfrac{t^{18}}{36}+C$

The given right side, in terms of $t$:

$\dfrac{1}{m}t^{n}\left (n\cdot \dfrac{t^{2}+1}{2t}-\dfrac{t^{2}-1}{2t}\right )=\dfrac{t^{n-1}}{2m}\left [(n-1)t^{2}+(n+1)\right ]=\dfrac{(n-1)t^{n+1}}{2m}+\dfrac{(n+1)t^{n-1}}{2m}$

Comparing powers, $n+1=20\Rightarrow n=19$. Comparing the coefficients of $t^{20}$, $\dfrac{18}{2m}=\dfrac{1}{40}\Rightarrow m=360$; the $t^{18}$ term agrees, since $\dfrac{20}{720}=\dfrac{1}{36}$.

$m+n=360+19=379$

Hence, the answer is 379.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift

text: A card from a pack of 52 cards is lost. From the remaining 51 cards, n cards are drawn and are found to be spades. If the probability of the lost card to be a spade is $\frac{11}{50}$, then n is equal to $________$ .
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let $L$ be the event that the lost card is a spade and $E$ the event that the $n$ cards drawn from the remaining 51 are all spades. Then $P(L)=\dfrac{1}{4}$ and $P(\bar{L})=\dfrac{3}{4}$.

If the lost card is a spade, 12 spades remain, so $P(E|L)=\dfrac{{}^{12}C_{n}}{{}^{51}C_{n}}$; otherwise 13 spades remain, so $P(E|\bar{L})=\dfrac{{}^{13}C_{n}}{{}^{51}C_{n}}$.

By Bayes' theorem,

$P(L|E)=\frac{\frac{1}{4}{}^{12}C_{n}}{\frac{1}{4}{}^{12}C_{n}+\frac{3}{4}{}^{13}C_{n}}=\frac{1}{1+3\cdot \dfrac{{}^{13}C_{n}}{{}^{12}C_{n}}}.$

Since $\dfrac{{}^{13}C_{n}}{{}^{12}C_{n}}=\dfrac{13!(12-n)!}{12!(13-n)!}=\dfrac{13}{13-n}$,

$P(L|E)=\frac{1}{1+\frac{39}{13-n}}=\frac{13-n}{52-n}.$

$\frac{13-n}{52-n}=\frac{11}{50}\Rightarrow 650-50n=572-11n\Rightarrow 39n=78\Rightarrow n=2$

Hence, the answer is 2.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift

text: Let the three sides of a triangle ABC be given by the vectors $2\hat{i}-\hat{j}+\hat{k},\hat{i}-3\hat{j}-5\hat{k}$ and $3\hat{i}-4\hat{j}-4\hat{k}$. Let $G$ be the centroid of the triangle $ABC$. Then $6\left (|\mathrm{AG}\leftarrow |^{2}+|\mathrm{BG}\leftarrow |^{2}+|\mathrm{CG}\leftarrow |^{2}\right )$ is equal to $__________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The given vectors satisfy $(2\hat{i}-\hat{j}+\hat{k})+(\hat{i}-3\hat{j}-5\hat{k})=3\hat{i}-4\hat{j}-4\hat{k}$, so take $AB\leftarrow =2\hat{i}-\hat{j}+\hat{k}$, $BC\leftarrow =\hat{i}-3\hat{j}-5\hat{k}$ and $AC\leftarrow =3\hat{i}-4\hat{j}-4\hat{k}$. The required sum is symmetric in $A$, $B$, $C$, so this labelling does not affect it.

For the centroid $G$: $AG\leftarrow =\dfrac{AB\leftarrow +AC\leftarrow }{3}$, $BG\leftarrow =\dfrac{BA\leftarrow +BC\leftarrow }{3}$, $CG\leftarrow =\dfrac{CA\leftarrow +CB\leftarrow }{3}$.

$AG\leftarrow =\dfrac{1}{3}(5\hat{i}-5\hat{j}-3\hat{k})\Rightarrow |AG\leftarrow |^{2}=\dfrac{25+25+9}{9}=\dfrac{59}{9}$

$BG\leftarrow =\dfrac{1}{3}(-\hat{i}-2\hat{j}-6\hat{k})\Rightarrow |BG\leftarrow |^{2}=\dfrac{1+4+36}{9}=\dfrac{41}{9}$

$CG\leftarrow =\dfrac{1}{3}(-4\hat{i}+7\hat{j}+9\hat{k})\Rightarrow |CG\leftarrow |^{2}=\dfrac{16+49+81}{9}=\dfrac{146}{9}$

$6\left (|AG\leftarrow |^{2}+|BG\leftarrow |^{2}+|CG\leftarrow |^{2}\right )=6\times \dfrac{59+41+146}{9}=6\times \dfrac{246}{9}=164$

Hence, the answer is 164.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift

text: If $α$ is a root of the equation $x^{2}+x+1=0$ and $\sum\limits _{\mathrm{k}=1}^{\mathrm{n}}\left (α^{\mathrm{k}}+\frac{1}{α^{\mathrm{k}}}\right )^{2}=20$, then n is equal to $_________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body: $\begin{array}{l} α\text{is root of equation}1+x+x^{2}=0,α=ω\text{or}ω^{2} \\ \begin{array}{l} \left (α^{k}+\dfrac{1}{α^{k}}\right )^{2}=α^{2k}+\dfrac{1}{α^{2k}}+2=ω^{k}+\dfrac{1}{ω^{k}}+2 \\ \Rightarrow ω^{k}+\dfrac{1}{ω^{k}}+2=\left \{\begin{array}{l} 4,3\text{divides}k \\ 1,3\text{does not divide}k \end{array} \\ \therefore \quad \sum\limits _{k=1}^{n}\left (α^{k}+\dfrac{1}{α^{k}}\right )^{2}=20 \\ \Rightarrow (1+1+4)+(1+1+4)+(1+1+4)+(1+1) \\ =20 \\ \Rightarrow n=11 \end{array} \end{array} \right.$
